The decision in one minute

Start with a practice that works for you.

01

Sell clear, bounded care

Pay-as-you-go appointments with a familiar GP, published sessions and a clear next step. Measure all care time, including work after the call.

02

Prove demand affordably

Test appropriate physiotherapy introductions and a simple booking route. Compare adults’ and families’ needs before choosing a lead audience.

03

Earn the right to expand

Membership and additional doctors are later options. Recurring payments do not guarantee profit or manageable clinical workload.

What success needs to show

Patients choose and pay for appropriate care. Fees cover full care time and overhead. Cash remains available. Follow-through is reliable and the diary is manageable.

Working scope: England first, subject to confirmation of actual service reach, registration conditions and clinical boundaries. This is an advisory plan, not launch approval.

What we need to know — and why each answer changes a decision

True cost and cash

How: Amal and accountant reconcile bank statements, invoices, subscriptions and commitments; build a 13-week cash view.

Why: Sets the spending ceiling and reveals what each appointment must contribute.

Real capacity

How: Amal records preparation, appointment, notes, messages, results and business time against her actual diary.

Why: Determines safe appointment volume and whether pricing pays for the work.

Paid demand

How: Short interviews plus source-tracked, suitable paid bookings; record why people decline.

Why: Chooses the audience and channel using behaviour rather than enthusiasm.

Delivery readiness

How: Amal reviews scope, contracts, cover, results ownership, privacy and public claims with relevant specialists.

Why: Defines what can safely be offered and promoted.

03 / Patients & the promise

Who is most likely to value a familiar GP?

Customer hypotheses · S1 §6

First test: suitable self-paying adults

People who value time, explanation and continuity; can use remote care; accept published sessions; and understand separately charged diagnostics or specialist care.

Test: Do they book at a sustainable fee, rather than use an existing employer benefit or another service?

Compare: parents and families

A trusted doctor may matter strongly. Demand, willingness to pay and the workload of supporting several family members remain unproven.

Boundary: Confirm age eligibility, consent, safeguarding and examination/escalation routes before promoting family care.

Proposed discovery: 12–15 short interviews across the leading groups, including users and nonbuyers. This is a learning sample, not a market-size estimate. Ask about the last real care decision before describing an offer.

The patient journey: trust becomes a reliable experience

Proposed design · S1 §11. Expand each stage for the practical commitment and measure.

01

Discover

“Is this for me?”

Clear scope and trusted introductions. Track eligible enquiries by source.

02

Consider

“Why pay?”

Explain clinician, time, fees and external costs. Record reasons to decline.

03

Trust

“Can I rely on it?”

Accurate credentials, limits and registration wording. Review claims.

04

Book

“Is it straightforward?”

Clear fees, sessions and suitability route. Measure eligible enquiry → paid booking.

05

Prepare

“What do you need?”

Secure history, identity, location and consent. Track incomplete preparation.

06

Consult

“Will I be heard?”

Appropriate assessment and shared plan. Record all care time.

07

Follow through

“Who owns the next step?”

Written plan and tracked results/referrals. Monitor overdue work.

08

Continue or refer

“What happens next?”

Appropriate follow-up or onward care. Measure repeat need and patient feedback.

The promise must fit the diary.

“Personal online GP care with Dr Amal, within published appointment sessions, with clear next steps.” This is proposed wording to validate. Do not imply unlimited access, guaranteed prescriptions, or a backup team that is not in place.

04 / Making the money understandable

A booking is income.
Profit depends on what it costs.

Revenue

The money charged for completed care. It does not tell you what is left.

Contribution

The fee minus the cost of delivering that care. This helps pay the practice’s running costs.

Profit and cash

Profit remains after all costs, including a fair value for your time. Cash is the money available when bills fall due; timing matters.

Illustrative calculator · not a forecast or tariff recommendation

Change the assumptions. See what the decision depends on.

Starting values illustrate a standard care episode from S1 §10: £79 fee, 30 minutes total care, £90/hour clinician time and £7 other direct cost. The £79 is a test hypothesis, not an approved offer.

Per-encounter contribution
Encounters to cover monthly costs
Illustrative monthly surplus

Read the calculation and its limits

Care cost = total care minutes ÷ 60 × hourly time value + other direct cost. Contribution = fee − care cost. Break-even encounters = monthly overhead and business-time cost ÷ contribution, rounded up. Surplus = completed encounters × contribution − monthly overhead and business-time cost.

The starting monthly cost of £1,583 combines illustrative £1,000 overhead, £433 business time and £150 acquisition cost (S1 §10). Change it to your actual total. Do not count the same cost twice. Include reserved availability, absence cover, extra care, refunds and other missing costs when relevant. Taxes, financing and historical investment recovery are excluded. A mixed clinic needs a separate time-and-cost calculation for each type of care.

The practical rule: If the required bookings exceed safe capacity, change the price, cost or proposition. More patients cannot rescue a loss on every consultation. Cash break-even also does not repay the earlier £50k+.

Why membership comes later

Membership brings predictable receipts, but also a promise of future work. Define included appointments, messages, response windows, exclusions, cover and cancellation terms. Measure actual use and repeat need first. Unlimited access is not recommended at this stage.

The week-eight decision

Continue, change or pause — using evidence.

Continue a controlled test if suitable paid care makes a positive contribution, demand is affordable to acquire, the diary is manageable and follow-through is reliable. Change the price, cost or channel if the model falls short. Pause expansion when care assurance, cash or delivery capacity is unresolved.

Proposed later expansion gate: three consecutive months of surplus after full costs and founder time, positive 13-week forward cash and maintained care quality. This is a management threshold, not proof of annual sustainability.

Five measures for the weekly review
  1. Cash: opening cash plus expected receipts minus payments over 13 weeks.
  2. Suitable demand: eligible enquiries → paid bookings → completed care, by channel.
  3. Contribution: full care cost and marketing cost against each completed encounter.
  4. Workload: all clinical and business hours, waiting time and available capacity.
  5. Care completion: every open result/referral has an owner and due date; Amal defines clinical tolerances and reviews failures.

Acquisition cost = attributable channel spending ÷ new paying patients from that channel. Booking conversion = paid bookings ÷ eligible enquiries. Record the period and small sample size; attribution is imperfect.

How the ten agreed actions fit

S2 p9 actions 1, 2, 5 and 7 become the financial and supplier review; 3 and 4 define scope and audience; 6 and 10 become controlled acquisition tests; 9 becomes this strategy and working plan. Action 8, clinician onboarding, remains a later expansion requirement, with absence cover reviewed now.

Care and trust / Readiness before wider promotion

Make the boundaries as clear as the benefits.

Amal owns clinical readiness

Confirm eligibility, physical patient location, remote suitability, prescribing, safeguarding, records, escalation, complaints and secure handover. Assign responsibility for results and referrals through completion, including absence.

GMC professional standards apply to remote care. CQC registration requirements concern regulated activity in England; verify the actual certificate, conditions and statement of purpose for the proposed service.

CQC registration ↗ · GMC prescribing ↗

Trustworthy marketing

Substantiate service claims and qualifications. Do not promise clinical outcomes or advertise prescription-only medicines to the public. Assess marketing permissions, tracking and data flows before campaigns; keep patient information out of marketing tools pending an appropriate assessment.

CAP is the advertising code; ICO guidance explains privacy and electronic-marketing requirements. These links do not establish i-doccare’s compliance.

06 / Amal + Artisan working review

Turn the discussion into evidence and decisions.

Use this workspace together while reviewing the overview. Start with the two Red areas, then confirm clinical and delivery readiness before widening promotion. Each area has a key question, evidence request, proposed responsibility and a condition for reducing the risk.

A provisional management view — not an audit.

Red: a material reported gap needs a decision or action now, before further discretionary spending or scale. Amber: evidence or controls remain incomplete; validate within an agreed boundary before expanding. Green: current evidence demonstrates agreed controls are working, with a named owner and review date.

No area starts Green because the available material does not establish operating effectiveness. Amber in clinical or regulatory areas means evidence is incomplete; it does not allege unsafe or unlawful care. Escalate any actual serious safety, legal or cash issue immediately to the appropriate accountable person.

Initial ratings are advisory judgments based on S1/S2 and the cited public record as at 16 October 2026. Impact is the potential consequence if the risk occurs. Likelihood is not established from the supplied evidence; no numerical risk score has been invented. An updated rating needs a reason and evidence, not just a colour change.

2 areas

Cash visibility and pricing economics.

Amber · validate

Demand, marketing, care, assurance, capacity, suppliers and management.

How to read the evidence labels

Verified: a linked primary public source supports the specific statement. Founder reported / estimate: recorded in the discussion, awaiting records. Hypothesis / illustrative: a proposition or calculation to test. Recommendation: the proposed next step based on available evidence.

Artisan Business Consulting / A fair basis for moving forward

Clarity before commitment.

Amal, you estimate that at least £50,000 has already been spent, without the commercial progress you expected. You deserve to understand what the next pound is intended to achieve.

Artisan’s proposed approach is grounded in equity and fairness: make uncertainty visible, explain the choices, agree proportionate work and judge suppliers by useful outcomes. The estimate is not an audited loss or proof that every past supplier delivered no value. We should establish what was bought, what remains useful and what can be stopped.

This overview is offered in that spirit: practical clarity, respect for your clinical experience and support for your independent business judgement. It creates no obligation to engage Artisan. Any future paid relationship should have separately agreed scope, fees, milestones and review points, while preserving your ownership and control.
